**Keeping a three‑year‑old smartwatch healthy for a few more years** Below are proven, low‑effort habits that address the most common wear‑and‑tear problems (battery decay, screen wear, water‑seal degradation, strap fatigue, and software glitches). The advice pulls directly from the wearables guidance we’ve compiled, especially the battery‑life and durability points from the “long‑battery wearable” session [[summaries/session-04_2024-06-15]]. | Area | What to Do | Why It Helps | |------|------------|--------------| | **Battery care** | • **Charge in the 20 %–80 % window** rather than letting the pack sit at 0 % or 100 % for long periods.
• **Avoid overnight “trickle‑charge”** on a full battery.
• **Store at ~50 % if you won’t wear it for weeks** (e.g., during a vacation). | Lithium‑ion cells age faster when repeatedly deep‑discharged or kept at high voltage. Keeping the charge in the mid‑range slows capacity loss, a point emphasized in the battery‑life‑optimization discussion of the Garmin‑focused session [[summaries/session-04_2024-06-15]]. | | **Screen protection** | • Use a **tempered‑glass protector** especially on AMOLED displays (which are power‑hungry but delicate).
• **Lower brightness** and **disable always‑on mode** when you can; this cuts power draw and reduces pixel wear. | Always‑on AMOLED screens consume the most power and can develop “burn‑in” over time. The same session notes that reducing brightness and avoiding constant screen‑on extends both battery and screen life. | | **Water‑resistance maintenance** | • Rinse the watch with fresh water after exposure to **salt water or chlorine** and dry it gently.
• **Don’t press buttons** while the watch is wet; let the seals dry first. | The seals that keep water out can degrade if salty or chlorinated water sits on them. Regular rinsing preserves the rating (e.g., 5 ATM) and prevents corrosion. | | **Strap & case wear** | • Rotate **replaceable straps** (silicone, leather, metal) every 6–12 months or when you notice cracks/weakening.
• Clean the band with mild soap and a soft cloth; avoid harsh chemicals. | Strap fatigue can cause the watch to slip or break. The durability checklist from the same session flags “scratch protection” and “water resistance” as key longevity factors. | | **Sensor & GPS usage** | • **Turn off GPS** when you’re not tracking a workout; use “phone‑only” location when possible.
• **Disable continuous night‑time SpO₂ or heart‑rate monitoring** if you don’t need them. | GPS and continuous sensor polling are major power drains and generate heat, which accelerates battery wear. The session recommends limiting night‑time SpO₂ and using standard GPS to reach 7‑10 day battery life. | | **Software updates** | • Keep the **firmware** up‑to‑date via the companion app.
• Occasionally **reset the device** (soft restart) to clear stale processes that can cause battery‑drain bugs. | Firmware patches often include battery‑optimisation tweaks and security fixes that keep the watch running smoothly. | | **Temperature control** | • **Avoid extreme heat** (leaving the watch on a dashboard, near a heater) and **extreme cold** (outside in sub‑0 °C for long periods).
• If the watch gets hot during a workout, let it cool before re‑charging. | High temperatures hasten lithium‑ion degradation; cold temperatures temporarily reduce capacity and can stress internal components. | | **Physical impact** | • **Store the watch in a soft case** when not worn to protect against knocks.
• **Avoid wearing it while doing heavy manual work** (e.g., hammering) that could bend the case or damage the sensors. | Mechanical stress can crack the housing or impair the accelerometer/gyroscope, leading to inaccurate tracking. | | **Regular cleaning** | • Wipe the **screen and case** with a lint‑free microfiber cloth weekly.
• Use a **cotton swab** lightly dampened to clean around the charging pins and sensors. | Dust and sweat can build up, causing false sensor readings and slowing down charging contacts. | ### Quick “daily checklist” 1. **Charge smartly** – 20 %→80 % when convenient. 2. **Check display settings** – brightness low, always‑on off. 3. **Sync & update** – run the companion app at least once a week. 4. **Wipe after sweat** – quick cloth wipe after workouts. 5. **Inspect straps & seals** – look for cracks or water‑spot buildup. By consistently applying these habits, the smartwatch’s battery, display, and overall hardware should stay reliable for another 2‑4 years, matching the longevity you’ve already enjoyed.

It’s generally wiser to **hold off on ordering a custom strap until you’ve locked in the exact device you’ll be wearing**.

- The strap you’re looking at is made for the **specific case shape, latch type and bezel size of the current watch or band**. If you later decide to switch to a different model (for example, moving from a fitness band to a full‑featured smartwatch, or swapping between Garmin’s LCD‑based Forerunner series and an AMOLED watch), the fit will change and the “custom” strap may no longer work.  

- The **“Smartwatch vs. Fitness Band”** concept stresses that choosing a device first is the primary step; only after you’ve settled on a hardware platform should you worry about accessories like straps. It notes that “select a device that matches your … notification needs” and that “hybrid approaches sit between the categories, offering enough smart functionality while preserving week‑long endurance.” Knowing which category (and thus which case) you need clarifies the strap dimensions you’ll require.  

- Custom straps often have **long lead times and limited return options**. Waiting lets you verify the exact model, confirm the strap‑mounting system (e.g., quick‑release pins, screw‑down lugs, or band‑type loops), and compare a few vendors for price and quality before committing.

**Bottom line:** finalize the wearable (smartwatch, fitness band, or hybrid) you’ll be using, confirm its case dimensions and attachment method, then order the custom strap. This avoids the risk of purchasing a strap that won’t fit later or that you’ll have to replace after a device upgrade.
